title: Judicial Pendency
lead: With over ==5.5 crore cases pending==, delay has become the single largest structural threat to the credibility of India's justice-delivery system — and to the constitutional promise of ==Article 21==.

Key indicator
rows: Working strength well below sanctioned in most HCs
Over ==1.8 crore== cases stuck at appearance/service alone

blocks.text: India's ==judge-to-population ratio was ~21 per million== (2022) — far below the ==50-per-million benchmark== of the Law Commission and the ==Justice V.S. Malimath Committee==. Source: NJDG; PRS Vital Stats.

items: ==Civil–criminal split==: at subordinate level ~==77% criminal, 23% civil==; the reverse in the SC (==79% civil, 21% criminal==).
==Government as litigant==: the State is a party in ==about 50% of all pending cases== — the single largest litigant.
==Land and property disputes==: ~==20% of all pending cases== and ==66% of pending civil cases==; about a quarter of matters decided by the SC.

==Age of pendency==: growth averaged ~2.8%/year (2010–2020); clearing the existing backlog with no new filings would take ~1.3 years (SC) and ~3 years each (HCs, subordinate courts) — an unrealistic counterfactual.
==Undertrial prisoners==: a large share of the prison population awaits trial — many ==beyond the maximum sentence== for the alleged offence (NCRB Prison Statistics).

items.title: Higher Judiciary
bullets: ==Constitution Bench backlog== — 5/7/9-judge matters wait years while regular benches are consumed by SLPs; subordinate courts stay proceedings awaiting authoritative rulings
==Litigation explosion via Art 136 SLPs== — special leave has expanded far beyond an exceptional remedy, turning the SC into a routine court of appeal
==Chronic HC vacancies== — protracted file movement between collegium, state and Union governments
==Adjournment culture== — weak enforcement of CPC limits, want of firm case management
==Fragmented case law and forum-shopping== — divergent HC rulings encourage repeat litigation

items.title: Lower Judiciary
bullets: ==Over 85% of all pendency== sits here — the true epicentre, and where citizens actually meet the system
==Infrastructure deficit== — courtroom space, understaffed registries, poor digitisation, shortages of court managers, translators, forensic support
==Investigation and prosecution delays== — late chargesheets, poor investigation quality, forensic backlogs, hostile witnesses
==Service of summons== — ==over 1.8 crore cases stuck merely at appearance/service==: a problem of process, not adjudication
==Multiplicity of proceedings== — parallel civil and criminal proceedings on the same facts
==Government litigation== — departments fail to decide timely on settlement, appeal or withdrawal

items.title: Strength & Appointments
bullets: Sanctioned strength ==34 → 38== judges — first increase since 2019
Steady collegium recommendations through 2026 — but many pending with the Centre; ==7 of 25 HCs under Acting Chief Justices== (July 2026)
==Advance-transfer policy (Feb 2026)== — CJ-designate transferred ~2 months before the vacancy

items.title: Technology & Administration
bullets: Reconstituted ==AI Committee (Dec 2025)==, chaired by Justice P.S. Narasimha
==Unified digital case-status platform (Jan 2026)== linking all three tiers in real time
==Four Special Division Benches (13 July 2026)== for the oldest matters — ~==800 legacy cases== for time-bound disposal
Continued emphasis on ==mediation and Lok Adalats== as the greatest immediate potential

items.title: Budget & Infrastructure
bullets: Union Budget 2026–27: ==₹2,010 crore== — ₹810 cr district/subordinate infrastructure + ==₹1,200 cr e-Courts Phase III==
==775 Fast Track Special Courts== incl. ==398 exclusive POCSO courts== — extended to September 2026

items.title: Proposals
bullets: ==‘Sahmati Samadhan Nyaya Mission’== — a national mission for negotiated justice, mainstreaming plea bargaining and pre-trial settlement (a policy proposal, not an announced scheme)

head: Country
Key mechanism
Design feature India can draw on
rows: Judges ==fix trial timelines at the first hearing==; scheduling software and cause-list discipline
==Court-annexed mediation/arbitration== built into civil procedure before trial is permitted
High judge ratio (~24+ per 100,000); ==written procedure== to shorten hearings
==Statutory deadlines== for categories of cases, centrally monitored

items.title: Strength & Appointments
bullets: ==Binding 3–6 month timeline== between collegium recommendation and notification, via a revised MoP
Move toward ==50 judges per million==, calibrated to each state's filing trends
Revive the ==All-India Judicial Service== with safeguards for state autonomy and reservation
==Strengthen the district cadre== — fast-track promotions, better service conditions

items.title: Court & Case Management
bullets: ==Differentiated case-flow management== — fast-track / standard / complex at filing (Australia)
==Enforce the CPC three-adjournment limit== with costs
==Extend special legacy benches== to HCs and district courts
==Restrain expansive Art 136 SLPs== — reserve the docket for genuine constitutional importance
==National uniform case-management rules==

items.title: ADR & Negotiated Justice
bullets: ==Mainstream plea bargaining== — from sub-1% usage toward the ==15–30%== of continental Europe, with anti-coercion safeguards
==Scale Lok Adalats and pre-litigation mediation== (matrimonial, MACT, cheque-bounce, commercial)
==Extend the Commercial Courts Act's mandatory pre-institution mediation== to wider civil and family disputes
==Reform lawyer remuneration== so settlement isn't penalised

items.title: Technology & Infrastructure
bullets: Deliver ==e-Courts Phase III== (₹7,210 crore, 2023–27) — paperless courts, virtual capacity, nationwide e-filing
==Responsible AI== for allocation, cause lists, translation, research — technology as ==‘a servant of justice, not its substitute’==
==Fix the summons bottleneck== — electronic, tracked service
Sustain ==district-court infrastructure funding==

items.title: Government Litigation & Criminal Justice
bullets: Implement the ==National Litigation Policy== — empower departments to withdraw frivolous appeals; ==litigation audits==
==Strengthen investigation quality== — forensics, trained IOs, time-bound chargesheets
==Undertrial Review Committees== and DLSAs active under ==s.479 BNSS== (old s.436A CrPC)
Make ==FTSC/POCSO courts permanent== and adequately funded

items.title: Institutional Measures
bullets: A statutory ==National Judicial Infrastructure Authority==
==Data-driven monitoring== — NJDG as a management tool with accountability for pendency targets
==Legislative correction of appeal-heavy laws== (taxation, land acquisition) to build finality earlier
